This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed seeking an order to set aside the award passed in MCOP No.52 of 2017, dated 19/01/2021 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Subordinate Judge,
Kuzhithurai.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Subordinate Judge,
Kuzhithurai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.The facts in brief:-
On 30/08/2011 at about 11.20 am, the petitioner was about to take a cup of tea in front of a tea shop on the western side of Kazhuvanthittai to Kuzhithurai road.

At that time, the first respondent vehicle driver drove the two wheeler bearing registration No.TN-75-A-6248 in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner,
causing injuries.
Because of the accidental injuries, he could not continue his work as before.
3.Over the occurrence, a case in Crime No.737 of 2011 was registered by the Kalliyakkavilai Police Station.
Claiming compensation of Rs.4,50,000/-, the claim petition has been filed.

4.That was resisted by the Insurance Company contending that the first respondent was not having proper driving licence; Apart from that, it is also stated that because of the rash and negligent act on the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis part of the claimant, the occurrence took place.
So both must take responsibility equally for the occurrence.
5.Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, 2 witnesses were examined and 28 documents marked.
On the side of the Insurance Company, one witness was examined and 6 documents marked.

The Disability Certificate issued by the District Medical Board has been marked as Ex.C1.
6.The Tribunal

on the basis of the evidence adduced and materials placed, came to the conclusion with regard to the first aspect of negligence that it occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent vehicle and fixed the responsibility upon the first respondent vehicle driver.

Regarding the compensation, it arrived at Rs.2,08,950/- under the following heads:-
Compensation of injuries Rs.1,20,000/-
 Pain and Sufferings Rs. 30,000/-

Medical Bills Rs. 51,950/-
 Nutrition expenses Rs. 5,000/-
 Transport Expenses Rs. 2,000/-

Total Rs.2,08,950/-

, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is preferred.
9.Heard both sides.
10.The only contention that was raised by the appellant is that the first respondent is the owner-cum- driver, was not having proper driving licence to drive the two wheeler.
He is referring to Ex.P13.
Wherein, we find that that he was issued with LMV, transport vehicle and non-transport vehicle.
but no separate licence was issued to drive the two wheeler.
11.The contention on the part of the appellant seems to be acceptable.
Without going through the records, the Tribunal has recorded a finding that he was issued with licence to drive the two wheeler.
When there is violation of Motor Vehicles Act and policy condition, naturally the first respondent has to bear the responsibility.
12.The next question is whether pay and recovery can be ordered.

13.Since the appellant is a third party to the contractual obligation between the appellant and the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis first respondent herein, as usual pay and recovery can be ordered by this court in this matter also.
14.Regarding the compensation as well as negligence, no argument was advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant.
So that portion of the finding is confirmed.

15.In the light of the above said discussion, due to the absence of the driving licence on the part of the first respondent, the appellant herein is directed to pay the entire compensation amount and recover the same from the second respondent herein.
To that extent, the award is modified.
16.In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed as indicated above.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed .
